questions.question: A tank is filled in 4 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and pipe B is thrice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Chain the three rates off A. 
B = 3A,   C = 2B = 6A   ⇒   A : B : C = 1 : 3 : 6 
 Step 2   Together they do 10 units an hour and 
finish in 4 hours. 
tank = 10 × 4 = 40 units 
 Step 3   A alone works at 1 unit an hour. 
40 / 1 = 40 hours

questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a tank in 6 hours and 16 hours, respectively. C is a filling pipe. All three pipes were opened together. They took 80 minutes to empty 5/18th of the tank. Pipe C alone can fill the tank in:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Turn the 80 minutes into an emptying 
rate. 
(5/18) of the tank in 4/3 hours   ⇒  rate = (5/18) 
÷ (4/3) = 5/24 per hour 
 Step 2   Write the net rate with C fighting the 
other two. 
1/6 + 1/16 − 1/c = 5/24 
 Step 3   Solve. 
11/48 − 1/c = 10/48   ⇒  1/c = 1/48   ∴  C fills in 48 
hours

questions.question: There are two water taps in a tank which can fill the empty tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively. There is a leakage point at the bottom which can empty the tank in 36 hours. If both taps are opened together and the leakage was repaired after 1 hour, in how much time will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Rates while the leak is open. 
1/12 + 1/18 − 1/36 = (3 + 2 − 1)/36 = 1/9 
 Step 2   So after one hour. 
1/9 filled,   8/9 still to go 
 Step 3   The leak is repaired, so the two taps 
alone finish it. 
(8/9) ÷ (5/36) = 32/5 = 6 h 24 min 
 Step 4   Add the first hour. 
1 h + 6 h 24 min = 7 hours 24 minutes

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours. Pipe B can fill the same tank in 12 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 16 hours. All pipes are opened at 8:00 AM. Pipe A and B are closed one hour's work — A : B : C = 1 : 3 : 6 A 1 B 3 C 6 10 units an hour x 4 hours = a 40-unit tank LEVEL - 3 simplicrack simplicrack Math simplicrack Maths MRQ SERIES SSC CGL 2026 at 10:00 AM. After how much time from starting will the tank be empty?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Rates per hour. 
A = 24,   B = 20,   C = −15 
 Step 2   8:00 to 10:00, all three run. 
(24 + 20 − 15) × 2 = 58 units in the tank 
 Step 3   A and B close; C empties alone. 
58 / 15 = 3 h 52 min 
 Step 4   Total from the start. 
2 h + 3 h 52 min = 5 hours 52 minutes
